questions.title: Greet Method With Name
questions.description:
Define a method greet(name) that prints "Hello, <name>!". Read a name from stdin and call greet with it.

Input Format:
A single line containing the name.

Output Format:
A single line "Hello, <name>!".

Constraints:
1 <= name length <= 50
questions.sourcecode:
def greet(name)
  puts "Hello, #{name}!"
end
greet(gets.chomp)

questions.title: Add Two Numbers Method
questions.description:
Define a method add(a, b) that returns a + b. Read two space-separated integers, call add, and print the result.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated integers a and b.

Output Format:
A single integer, a + b.

Constraints:
-10000 <= a, b <= 10000
questions.sourcecode:
def add(a, b)
  a + b
end
a, b = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
puts add(a, b)

questions.title: Default Greeting Method
questions.description:
Define a method greet(name = "Guest") that prints "Hi, <name>!". Read a string s. If s equals "default", call greet with no arguments (use the default); otherwise call greet(s).

Input Format:
A single line containing s.

Output Format:
A single line "Hi, <name>!" using either the default or the provided name.

Constraints:
1 <= s length <= 50
questions.sourcecode:
def greet(name = "Guest")
  puts "Hi, #{name}!"
end
s = gets.chomp
if s == "default"
  greet
else
  greet(s)
end

questions.title: Order Item Method With Keywords
questions.description:
Define a method order(item:, qty:) that prints "<qty> x <item>". Read a single line containing an item name and a quantity separated by a space, then call order with the corresponding keyword arguments.

Input Format:
A single line "item qty" where item is a single word and qty is an integer.

Output Format:
A single line "<qty> x <item>".

Constraints:
1 <= qty <= 1000; 1 <= item length <= 30
questions.sourcecode:
def order(item:, qty:)
  puts "#{qty} x #{item}"
end
parts = gets.split
item = parts[0]
qty = parts[1].to_i
order(item: item, qty: qty)

questions.title: Sum All Method With Splat
questions.description:
Define a method sum_all(*nums) that returns the sum of all arguments passed. Read n then n space-separated integers, call sum_all with the splatted array, and print the result.

Input Format:
First line: integer n.
Second line: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
A single integer, the sum of all n integers.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000; -10000 <= value <= 10000
questions.sourcecode:
def sum_all(*nums)
  total = 0
  nums.each { |n| total += n }
  total
end
n = gets.to_i
arr = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
puts sum_all(*arr)

questions.title: Discount Calculator With Default Percentage
questions.description:
Define a method discount(price, percent = 10) that returns the discounted price price * (100 - percent) / 100. Read price and percent. If percent is 0, call discount(price) to use the default 10 percent; otherwise call discount(price, percent). Print the result. Do not use case, when, or the ternary operator.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated integers price and percent.

Output Format:
A single integer, the discounted price.

Constraints:
1 <= price <= 100000; 0 <= percent <= 100
questions.sourcecode:

end
p, pct = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
if pct == 0
  puts discount(p)
else

end

questions.title: Email Compose Method With Keywords
questions.description:
Define a method compose(to:, subject:, body:) that returns a single string "To: <to> | Subject: <subject> | Body: <body>". Read three lines (to, subject, body). Call compose with keyword arguments and print the returned string. Do not use class or module.

Input Format:
Three lines: to, subject, then body.

Output Format:
A single line in the format "To: <to> | Subject: <subject> | Body: <body>".

Constraints:
1 <= each line length <= 100
questions.sampleoutput1: To: alice@example.com | Subject: Hello | Body: How are you?
questions.sampleoutput2: To: bob@x.com | Subject: Test | Body: Hi
questions.output1: To: a@b.com | Subject: Sub | Body: Msg
questions.output2: To: x@y.com | Subject: A | Body: B
questions.output3: To: p@q.com | Subject: Hello | Body: World
questions.sourcecode:
def compose(to:, subject:, body:)
  "To: #{to} | Subject: #{subject} | Body: #{body}"
end
to = gets.chomp
subject = gets.chomp
body = gets.chomp
puts compose(to: to, subject: subject, body: body)

questions.title: Largest Of Numbers With Splat Method
questions.description:
Define a method largest_of(*nums) that uses a loop to find the largest value among the arguments and returns it. Read n then n integers, call largest_of with the splatted array, and print the result. Do not use the built-in .max method, sort, or max as a substring.

Input Format:
First line: integer n.
Second line: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
A single integer, the largest value.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000; -10000 <= value <= 10000
questions.sourcecode:
def largest_of(*nums)
  best = nums.first
  nums.each do |n|
    best = n if n > best
  end
  best
end
count = gets.to_i
arr = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
puts largest_of(*arr)

questions.title: Config Override With Double Splat
questions.description:
Define a method invoice(amount, **taxes) that returns the amount plus the sum of all tax values. Read an amount, then n, then n key=value lines (value is an integer). Build a hash and call invoice with the double-splatted hash. Print the result. Do not use class or module.

Input Format:
First line: integer amount.
Second line: integer n.
Next n lines: each of the form "key=value".

Output Format:
A single integer, amount plus the sum of all tax values.

Constraints:
0 <= amount <= 1000000; 0 <= n <= 20; 0 <= value <= 10000
questions.sourcecode:
def invoice(amount, **taxes)
  total = amount
  taxes.each_value { |v| total += v }
  total
end
amount = gets.to_i
n = gets.to_i
opts = {}
n.times do
  k, v = gets.chomp.split("=")
  opts[k.to_sym] = v.to_i
end
puts invoice(amount, **opts)

questions.title: Counter Method With Local Scope
questions.description:
Define a method bump(counter, delta) that uses an explicit return to return counter + delta. Maintain an outer variable total starting at 0. Read n then n delta values. After each delta, set total = bump(total, delta) and print the new total. Do not use global ($total) or instance (@total) variables.

Input Format:
First line: integer n.
Second line: n space-separated integer deltas.

Output Format:
n lines, each containing the running total after applying that delta.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000; -10000 <= delta <= 10000
questions.sourcecode:
def bump(counter, delta)
  return counter + delta
end
total = 0
n = gets.to_i
deltas = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
deltas.each do |d|
  total = bump(total, d)
  puts total
end

questions.title: Eligibility Check Method With Early Return
questions.description:
Define a method eligible?(age, score) that returns "yes" if age >= 18 AND score >= 60, otherwise "no". Use early return statements for the failure cases. Read age and score, call eligible?, and print the result. Do not use case or when.

A single line with two space-separated integers age and score.

questions.title: Fibonacci Method With Memo Hash
questions.description:
Define a method fib(n, memo = {}) that returns the n-th Fibonacci number where fib(1) = 1, fib(2) = 1, fib(3) = 2, and so on. Use early return for n <= 2, and memoize using the hash argument. Read n and print fib(n). Do not use while, until, or for.

Input Format:
A single integer n.

Output Format:
A single integer, the n-th Fibonacci number.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 30
questions.sourcecode:
def fib(n, memo = {})
  return 1 if n <= 2
  return memo[n] if memo.key?(n)
  memo[n] = fib(n - 1, memo) + fib(n - 2, memo)
end
n = gets.to_i
puts fib(n)

questions.title: Bank Account Transaction Method
questions.description:
A bank account starts with balance B. Define methods deposit(balance, amount) which returns balance + amount, and withdraw(balance, amount) which returns balance - amount, or returns balance unchanged if amount exceeds the current balance (use an early return for that case). Read B, then n, then n transaction lines each "deposit X" or "withdraw X". Apply each transaction in order and print the final balance. Do not use class or instance variables.

Input Format:
First line: integer B.
Second line: integer n.
Next n lines: each "deposit X" or "withdraw X" with integer X.

Output Format:
A single integer, the final balance.

Constraints:
0 <= B <= 1000000; 1 <= n <= 100; 0 <= X <= 1000000
questions.sourcecode:
def deposit(balance, amount)
  return balance + amount
end
def withdraw(balance, amount)
  return balance if amount > balance
  balance - amount
end
balance = gets.to_i
n = gets.to_i
n.times do
  op, amt_str = gets.split
  amt = amt_str.to_i
  if op == "deposit"
    balance = deposit(balance, amt)
  else
    balance = withdraw(balance, amt)
  end
end
puts balance

questions.title: Tax Calculator With Double Splat Brackets
questions.description:
Define a method tax(income, **rates) where rates is a hash mapping a bracket name to a percent integer. The tax owed is income * total_rate / 100 where total_rate is the sum of all rate values. Read income, then n, then n lines of "name=percent". Build a hash and call tax with the double-splatted hash. Print the result. Do not use class or case.

Input Format:
First line: integer income.
Second line: integer n.
Next n lines: each "name=percent" with integer percent.

Output Format:
A single integer, the tax owed.

Constraints:
0 <= income <= 10000000; 0 <= n <= 20; 0 <= percent <= 100
questions.sourcecode:
def tax(income, **rates)
  total_rate = 0
  rates.each_value { |r| total_rate += r }
  income * total_rate / 100
end
income = gets.to_i
n = gets.to_i
opts = {}
n.times do
  k, v = gets.chomp.split("=")
  opts[k.to_sym] = v.to_i
end
puts tax(income, **opts)

questions.title: Text Processor With Multiple Methods
questions.description:
Define three methods. count_words(text) returns the number of whitespace-separated words in text. count_vowels(text) returns the number of vowels (a, e, i, o, u, case-insensitive) using each_char to iterate. longest_word(text) returns the longest word in text, returning the first one in case of ties, using each to iterate over the words. Read a line of text, call all three methods, and print each result on its own line. Do not use .max, .min, sort, or scan.

Input Format:
A single line of text.

Output Format:
Three lines: word count, vowel count, longest word.

Constraints:
1 <= text length <= 1000
questions.sourcecode:
def count_words(text)
  words = text.split
  words.size
end
def count_vowels(text)
  vowels = 0
  text.each_char do |c|
    if "aeiouAEIOU".include?(c)
      vowels += 1
    end
  end
  vowels
end
def longest_word(text)
  words = text.split
  best = words[0]
  words.each do |w|
    if w.length > best.length
      best = w
    end
  end
  best
end
text = gets.chomp
puts count_words(text)
puts count_vowels(text)
puts longest_word(text)
